title: GreenShield Health Insurance
fit_question: Describe a time when you led a team through significant change or introduced a new idea. Tell me about a time when you failed.
prompt: GreenShield Health Insurance wants to expand into Florida and needs a business plan to determine whether the market is attractive, which customers to target and which distribution channels to use.
interviewer_notes: Three-part interviewer-led case: market attractiveness and breakeven, channel selection, then recommendation. Discuss what a business plan must establish before asking for a framework. Show Exhibits 1 and 2 for market sizing and breakeven, then Exhibit 3 for channel economics.

suggested_framework.summary: Assess Florida's addressable segments and competition, entry economics, channel acquisition economics and GHI fit.

children.label: Policy price, medical and admin contribution
Upfront investment, scale and breakeven share
Direct and indirect channel leads, yield and cost
Capabilities, customer fit and execution risks

stages.interviewer_asks: What must GHI believe for a Florida entry to make sense?
stages.expected_answer: Florida must offer a large, growing and reachable customer pool, attractive policy contribution and attainable breakeven share; competition and regulation must be manageable; and GHI must have channels and capabilities that can acquire the target customers economically.

stages.interviewer_asks: How large is the target audience in Exhibit 1?
stages.expected_answer: Of 12M Florida adults, 6M lack employer coverage. Of these, 4.8M are insured and 1.2M uninsured. Thirty percent of the uninsured can afford coverage, or 360K, while 30% of the insured are unhappy, or 1.44M. The stated target audience is 1.8M.

stages.interviewer_asks: Using Exhibit 2, what volume and share are required to recover the $2M investment?
stages.expected_answer: Contribution per lifetime policy is $500-$350-$100=$50. Breakeven requires $2M/$50=40,000 policies. That is 0.833% of the 4.8M currently insured market used by the book, or 2.22% of the explicitly defined 1.8M target audience.
good_answer_signals: States the denominator for market share

stages.interviewer_asks: Which acquisition channels in Exhibit 3 are most attractive?
stages.expected_answer: Profit is $75K internet, $100K direct mail, $200K call center, $0 billboard and $1.95M agents. Agents dominate because 30% yield overcomes lower $750 revenue per sale and $30 lead cost; call centers and direct mail are next.
good_answer_signals: Calculates sales, revenue and lead cost by channel
Selects agents on profit rather than yield alone

stages.interviewer_asks: Should GHI enter Florida, and how?
stages.expected_answer: Enter because breakeven requires only 40,000 policies, 0.83% of the current insured base, and the modeled channels can be profitable. Lead with agents, then call centers and direct mail. Validate trends, target-channel fit, regulations and GHI's direct-sales capabilities before building the salesforce.
good_answer_signals: Links channel choice to capability and target fit risks

exhibits.title: Florida Market Sizing
exhibits.description: Florida adult, non-employer-covered, insured, uninsured, affordability and dissatisfaction inputs.
exhibits.key_insight: Affordable uninsured adults plus unhappy insured adults create a 1.8M target audience.

exhibits.title: Breakeven Inputs
exhibits.description: Upfront investment and lifetime per-policy revenue, medical cost and administrative cost.
exhibits.key_insight: Each policy contributes $50 toward the $2M upfront investment.

exhibits.title: Lead Generation by Channel
exhibits.description: Cost, lead volume, yield and revenue per sale for five acquisition channels.
exhibits.key_insight: Agents have by far the highest modeled acquisition profit due to a 30% yield.

math.question: How many policies and what share are required to break even?
math.answer: 40,000 policies; 0.83% of the current insured market or 2.22% of the stated target audience

math.question: What is modeled profit by acquisition channel?
givens: Exhibit 3 lead, yield, revenue and cost inputs
math.answer: $75K internet; $100K direct mail; $200K call center; $0 billboard; $1.95M agents

synthesis: Enter Florida, subject to validation. Breakeven is 40,000 policies—0.83% of the 4.8M currently insured base and 2.22% of the 1.8M defined target audience. Agents generate $1.95M in the channel model, followed by call centers and direct mail. Confirm market trends, regulations, target-channel fit and GHI's ability to build and manage direct sales.
what_great_looks_like: Selects channels on profit and tests strategic fit
common_pitfalls: Uses all Florida residents as the addressable market
Divides investment by revenue instead of contribution
Ranks channels only by lead volume or yield

extraction.notes: All exhibits use candidate-facing pages and their data fields contain inputs only. The book's 0.8% share uses the 4.8M currently insured denominator; 2.22% of the stated 1.8M target audience is also reported for clarity. Reviewed and accepted by Claude 2026-09-30.
